narrative.text: Continues the French AIDS resolution, voicing concern at the pandemic's fast spread in developing countries and some urban areas and stating that public health concerns cannot justify measures, such as mandatory screening, that violate individual rights. It endorses the 1992 update of the global strategy, which adds emphasis on treating other sexually transmitted diseases, improving the status of women and creating a supportive social environment. It closes with requests to fight discrimination and support national laws protecting the rights of people with HIV.

A French-language Executive Board resolution (EB89.R19, January 1992) on the global AIDS strategy, which thanks the Director-General for his report and notes WHO's leadership, its support to national programmes and wider UN mobilization. It recommends a resolution to the Forty-fifth World Health Assembly recalling earlier Assembly and UN General Assembly resolutions on AIDS.
